basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 2.' and it opens 'Vers. 2. Terra autem inanis et vacua. Id est, inutilis, infructuosa et incomposita. Omnia'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 2. Terra autem inanis et vacua. Id est, inutilis, infructuosa et incomposita. Omnia enim elementa commista erant et confusa, et totum hoc aeris spatium quod est a terra usque ad coelum plenum erat aquis, quae tamen non erant ejusmodi qualitatis cujus nunc sunt, sed in modum nubium tenues, | quam qualitatem adhuc illae supercoelestes aquae retinent. Spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas. Sicut mens vel sapientia alicujus artificis superfertur operi quod facturus est, ut quomodo vult ita illud faciat: ita et Spiritus sanctus superferebatur, praeordinans et quasi disponens quid, qualiter facere vellet.
